channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: 33/11 kV Substation: Single Line Diagram & Equipment Overview
item.description: How a 33/11 kV substation is built, walked through its single line diagram from incoming line to distribution feeders — every major equipment item, its function, and the protection schemes that back it up.

item.title: Essential Protection Settings of Air Circuit Breakers (ACB) Explained
item.description: LTPU, LTD, STPU, STD, instantaneous and ground fault settings on an Air Circuit Breaker (ACB) — what each protection parameter does, typical setting ranges, and why the settings exist as a coordinated set, not individual dials.

item.title: Access Control System (ACS) Explained: Components, Architecture & Site Work
item.description: How an Access Control System actually works — main components, the six-step credential-to-unlock sequence, system architecture, integration with FAS/BMS/CCTV, and what an electrical site engineer does on an ACS install.

item.title: ATS, MTS, ECB & Switch Disconnectors: Transfer & Isolation Switching Devices Explained
item.description: ATS, MTS, COS, switch disconnectors, load break switches, fused switch disconnectors, ECBs, maintenance bypass switches and key interlocks — what each device does, how it differs, and where it's used.

item.title: Column Axial Capacity: Why Reinforcement Ratio and Slenderness Both Matter
item.description: How gross area and steel ratio combine into a short column's axial capacity, why codes cap reinforcement ratio at both ends, and when slenderness cuts that capacity down.

item.title: Concrete Volume Takeoff: From Cubic Meters to Bags of Cement
item.description: How a concrete volume gets converted into cement, sand and aggregate quantities using mix ratios, why wastage factors are added, and what water-cement ratio does to the mix.

item.title: Cut & Fill Volume: How the Average End Area Method Actually Works
item.description: How earthwork volume between two cross-sections is estimated by averaging their areas, why section spacing controls accuracy, and where the method breaks down.

item.title: Electrical Panel Factory Acceptance Test (FAT): The Complete Checklist
item.description: The 8 stages of an LV panel FAT — visual and mechanical inspection, insulation resistance, hi-pot, functional, protection and interlock tests, and documentation — plus the acceptance criteria that close it out.

item.title: MCB, MCCB, ACB, RCCB & More: Electrical Switchgear & Protection Devices Explained
item.description: MCB, MCCB, ACB, VCB, SF6 breakers, RCCB, RCBO, ELCB, isolators, contactors, relays, fuses, SPDs and busbars — what each device does, how it differs, and where it's used.

item.title: FM-200, Novec 1230, CO2 & Foam: Fire Suppression Systems Explained
item.description: FM-200, Novec 1230, CO2 and foam fire suppression systems compared — components, applications, discharge time, ozone depletion and global warming potential, plus which NFPA standard applies to each.

item.title: Grade & Slope: Why Percent, Ratio and Degrees Aren't the Same Number
item.description: How rise over run converts between percent grade, a ratio like 1:20, and an angle in degrees — and why mixing up the three is a common site-drawing mistake.

item.title: HVAC MEP Thumb Rules & Formulas: Quick Reference for Engineers
item.description: Preliminary-design thumb rules for cooling load, airflow, fan and pump power, chilled water flow, chiller capacity, cooling tower sizing, and pipe sizing — with the formula behind each one.

item.title: HVAC & Plumbing Default Design Values: The Quick Reference
item.description: Common default design values for HVAC and plumbing — duct and pipe velocities, pressure drops, ACH, noise criteria, fresh air rates, temperatures, and plumbing velocities, pressures and slopes — for a first-pass sizing check.

item.title: IECEx / ATEX Zones vs NEC Class & Division: Hazardous Area Classification
item.description: How the IEC 60079 / ATEX Zone system (Zone 0/1/2, 20/21/22) compares to the North American NEC Class & Division system — equivalency table, gas/dust groups, temperature classes and Ex protection types explained.

item.title: Junction Boxes Explained: Types, Parts & Ratings
item.description: What a junction box actually does, the main types — pull box, gang box, weatherproof, explosion-proof, conduit body, terminal box, panel enclosure — its parts, a material and rating reference, box-fill sizing, and a selection checklist.

item.title: Motor Starting Methods: DOL vs Star-Delta vs Soft Starter vs VFD Compared
item.description: Why starting current matters, how DOL, star-delta, soft starters and VFDs each tame it differently, and a side-by-side comparison of current, torque, cost and complexity.

item.title: Manning's Equation: How Pipe Slope, Roughness and Diameter Set Flow Capacity
item.description: How Manning's equation turns pipe slope, roughness and diameter into gravity flow capacity, why full-bore isn't peak capacity, and what the roughness coefficient actually represents.

item.title: Rebar Development Length: Why Bar Diameter Decides the Embedment, Not Rules of Thumb
item.description: Why development length is a function of bar diameter and concrete/steel strength rather than a flat number, how lap splices scale off it, and what hooks buy you.

item.title: Slab-on-Grade Thickness: What Actually Drives the Number
item.description: Why slab-on-grade thickness comes from load, subgrade support and concrete strength together — not a flat default — and why the subgrade matters as much as the slab itself.

item.title: Staircase Geometry: The Riser-Tread Rule That Keeps Stairs Walkable
item.description: Why comfortable stairs come down to one relationship between riser height and tread depth, the typical ranges each falls within, and where headroom and going length come in.

item.title: System Voltages Explained: Low, Medium & High Voltage Levels and Phases
item.description: Voltage classification from ELV to UHV explained — IEC vs IEEE ranges, standard system voltages used worldwide, and single-phase vs three-phase configurations.

item.title: Trench Safe Slope: Why OSHA Soil Type Decides the Angle, Not the Depth
item.description: Why the same trench depth needs a completely different sloping angle depending on soil classification, what separates Type A, B and C soil, and when sloping stops being enough.

item.title: Industrial Valves Explained: Types & Parts
item.description: What a valve actually does, the main types — gate, globe, ball, butterfly, check, plug, needle, diaphragm, pressure relief — its parts, a materials and actuation reference, a selection checklist, and common failure points.

item.title: Password Entropy Explained: What Actually Makes a Password Hard to Crack
item.description: What password entropy actually measures, why length beats complexity rules, and how the math behind brute-force cracking time works.

item.title: Percentage Points vs Percent Change: Why They're Not the Same Number
item.description: Why 'up 5 percentage points' and 'up 5 percent' are two different numbers, and how mixing them up leads to real reporting errors.

item.title: Solar Payback Period & ROI: What the Simple Formula Leaves Out
item.description: Why simple payback (cost divided by annual savings) overstates solar economics, and what degradation, escalating electricity prices, and O&M costs actually do to the real payback.

item.title: Solar System Sizing: From Daily Load to Panel Count
item.description: How to go from a daily energy load in kWh to an array size in kW, why peak sun hours (not daylight hours) is the number that matters, and where the derating factors go.

item.title: Battery SoC vs DoD: Why They're Not the Same Number
item.description: Why SoC and DoD are two views of the same battery, how SoC is actually estimated in the field, and why chemistry sets the DoD limit that protects cycle life.

item.title: Row Spacing & Inter-Row Shading: Sizing the Gap Between Solar Rows
item.description: Why ground-mount and rooftop solar rows need a minimum gap, how the winter-solstice sun angle sets that gap, and the ground coverage ratio trade-off behind it.

item.title: String vs Microinverter vs Power Optimizer: Choosing a Solar Inverter Topology
item.description: How string inverters, microinverters and power optimizers actually differ in where MPPT happens, what a shaded panel costs you under each, and how to pick between them.
